bull_bear.body: Rs. 4,802 cr allocated to Exide Energy (Li-ion subsidiary); no dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on capex over shareholder returns; HDFC Life stake mark-to-market loss of Rs. 850 cr routed to OCI, no sale
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Commodity volatility (sulfur, plastic, LPG, lead, lithium); rupee depreciation; geopolitical disruption to exports; lithium-ion yield ramp-up delays; OEM contract lag in price pass-through; government policy delay for PLI/incentives
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on core business resilience, cautiously optimistic on macro, strongly committed to Make in India Li-ion, proactive on price hikes, transparent on challenges, seeking policy support
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Sulfuric acid cost surge is tied to petrochemical refinery utilization (sulfur byproduct), not just demand; Exide’s Li-ion pricing strategy hinges on China’s VAT hike (9% increase by Jan 2027) and localization incentives; Telecom decline is structural, not cyclical — Li-ion replacement is permanent; 92% of business grew double-digit despite 8% decline in exports/Telecom
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Domestic business ex-Telecom grew 16% in Q4; 2W/4W OEM: +25% YoY (2nd straight quarter); Home UPS: record Q4 sales; Solar: crossed Rs. 1,000 cr annual revenue; Industrial UPS ex-Telecom: double-digit growth; Exports: declined due to geopolitics; Telecom & E-Rickshaw: shifting to Li-ion
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin down 90 bps QoQ to 30.1% due to Rs. 150 cr net commodity impact; EBITDA margin held at 11.7% via cost controls, warranty reduction, and manufacturing excellence; sulfuric acid up 5x (Rs. 15/kg to Rs. 75/kg); plastic and LPG also pressured; price hikes implemented in Jan, Mar, Apr (cumulative 5-6%, April hike: 3%)
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: high single-digit to early double-digit YoY for FY27 core business; margin: EBITDA to be sustained via price hikes and cost controls; order inflow: strong in industrial UPS, railways, solar; capex/commissioning: Rs. 1,400 cr planned for FY27; cylindrical Li-ion trials starting May 2026, prismatic trials by June-July 2026
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Healthy order inflow in railways, motive power, industrial UPS; no specific value disclosed
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Lithium-ion cell manufacturing (6 GW capacity: 3 GW cylindrical for 2W/3W EVs, 3 GW prismatic for 4W EVs, BESS, Telecom); solar vertical scaling; export recovery in EU/US; industrial UPS demand from data centers and BESS
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Exide delivered record Q4 revenue and expanded EBITDA margin despite severe commodity inflation, driven by strong domestic demand across auto OEM, UPS, and solar verticals; the company is now pivoting to lithium-ion cell manufacturing with Rs. 4,802 cr invested, positioning itself as India’s first integrated Li-ion producer to capture EV and stationary storage growth, while navigating volatile input costs through staged price hikes and OEM contract renegotiations.

open.item: The Board recommended a final dividend of 200% (Rs 2 per equity share of Rs 1 face value) for FY 2025-26, a payout ratio of 15.3% of PAT, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM.
EESL's cylindrical line (for 2-wheelers) is under internal validation, with customer sample supplies expected in the next few months.

Through wholly-owned subsidiary EESL, Exide is developing a greenfield lithium-ion cell manufacturing facility at the Hi-Tech Defence & Aerospace Park (Phase-II), Bengaluru, on an 80-acre site with planned capacity of 12 GWh in two phases of 6 GWh each; sample deliveries and initial commercialisation are targeted for FY 2026-27.

EESL's prismatic lithium-ion cell line is close to starting sample production, with commissioning targeted in FY 2026-27; initial commercial dispatches to OEMs are also expected to commence in FY 2026-27.

EESL's greenfield lithium-ion cell manufacturing facility in Bengaluru (80-acre site, 12 GWh planned capacity across two 6 GWh phases) continues to progress toward commissioning, with the cylindrical 2-wheeler line's customer sample supplies expected within a few months and the prismatic line's commissioning targeted for FY 2026-27.

risks.note: Potential disruptions from geopolitical uncertainties, regulatory realignments, cross-border trade restrictions, tariff changes and market volatility; flagged as a HIGH severity risk affecting the Company's manufacturing footprint, supply chain and cost competitiveness.

Challenges in aligning operations with environmental standards (emissions, water use, waste handling) alongside evolving ESG regulatory requirements; flagged as a HIGH severity risk tied to Economic Performance and Risk Management & Compliance.

External economic variables and sectoral factors may hinder cash generation and impact capital availability, a MODERATE severity risk mitigated through a debt-free capital structure, strong credit ratings and disciplined treasury practices.

Fluctuating raw material costs (principally lead, benchmarked to LME rates) affect cost structure, availability and margins, and expose the Company to longer delivery cycles; a MODERATE severity risk mitigated via sourcing diversification, inventory management, pricing/indexation clauses and increased use of recycled lead.

Cyber intrusions, data breaches and malicious attacks pose risk to operations, data integrity and brand trust; a MODERATE severity risk mitigated through a 24/7 Security Operations Center, VAPT assessments and simulation drills.

Inability to adapt to evolving battery technology (e.g., the lead-acid to lithium-ion transition) can impact competitiveness, product relevance, market share and customer expectations; a MODERATE severity risk being addressed through technology collaborations and expansion into electric mobility.
